newsitem.title: USA: Overnight rain plus more due to keep Midwest wet.
newsitem.headline: Overnight rain plus more due to keep Midwest wet.

text.p: Overnight rain in Nebraska and southwest Iowa, plus more likely through Saturday should make many Midwest fields too wet to plant, a meteorologist said.

Up to an inch of rain fell late Tuesday and early Wednesday in eastern Nebraska and Iowa, said Joel Burgio, meteorologist with Weather Services Corp. Also, 0.50 to 1.5 inches were forecast for southern and eastern Iowa, northern Illinois and Wisconsin Wednesday and early Thursday, he said
"It is a relatively narrow area, but it will be very good coverage," said Burgio, who expects 70 to 80 percent coverage.
Nebraska grain dealers said the overnight rain plus the additional amounts forecast should halt planting for a while.
"It should slow planting activity considerably," in Nebraska, Iowa and northern Illinois, said Burgio.

Farmers in Missouri, central and southern Illinois, Indiana, and Ohio may be able to plant through Thursday, and then should be washed out Friday and Saturday when rainfall of 0.3 to 1.5 inches was forecast, said Burgio.
The second storm system will originate in the High Plains, late Thursday and should produce 0.25 to 1.00 inch of rain across the eastern half of Kansas.
Hail, high wind, and possibly tornadoes may accompany the Kansas storms, he said.
The dry western areas of Kansas received less than 0.25 inch late Tuesday and may receive another 0.25 inch from Thursday's storms.
Burgio said year-to-date rainfall in Goodland in northwest Kansas was 1.80 inches versus normal of 3.22 inches.
Temperatures from Kansas east across the Midwest should average below normal through the week, but not cold enough to harm crops, he said.
